reviews.text:
About four years ago, I took my pet budgie to the vet because it wasn't feeling well.

I was given medicine, but it died about three days later.

I think that vet clinic doesn't treat birds. Bird owners should avoid going there.
Thank you for submitting your review of our hospital.

When I visited the hospital without an appointment, I felt anxious because I had to wait a long time and was directed to another hospital.

However, later, the hospital director explained the situation to me by phone and letter, and I understood the hospital's circumstances.

I am always grateful for the careful examinations I receive from the hospital director. I look forward to your continued support.
They are very kind and I can leave it to them with peace of mind.

For about a year and a half, we treated him for blood in the urine, diarrhea, and health checkups. Compared to our previous veterinary clinic, we were always grateful that the examinations were less stressful for both our dog and us. We owe this to the prompt, careful, and, above all, gentle veterinarians and nurses.

Unfortunately, our dog passed away at the age of 17 years and 4 months.

At the end of the year, we were diagnosed with a serious condition, and there was a time when we resigned ourselves to the fact that he might not survive the new year, but thanks to the generous support of the doctors and nurses, we were able to spend over a month saying our precious goodbyes.

We received letters of condolence afterwards, and we were treated with such warmth until the very end, for which we are truly grateful. Thank you so much.

My 16-year-old cat recently became ill, and I took her to this vet for the first time. She was diagnosed with severe anemia and needed a blood transfusion, but they didn't perform them here. The vet gave us various advice, administered injections, and prescribed medication before we left.

However, the next morning, she was having trouble breathing, so I consulted this vet again. They recommended another hospital that likely performs blood transfusions and told me to call anytime if anything else happened.

I went to the hospital they recommended, and thankfully, my cat's life was saved. I am incredibly grateful to this vet. I also spoke with them on the phone afterward, and they were very kind and listened attentively, which I really appreciated.

Thank you so much for everything.

I am truly grateful.

Thank you, vet and nurses!

I received excellent care at your clinic several years ago when I had a hamster. The reception staff, the small animal specialists, and even the head veterinarian in the dog and cat room (whom I occasionally saw) were all incredibly kind. I feel I've found the best animal hospital I could have asked for. My female hamster was diagnosed with a uterine disease and spent most of her life battling it, but thanks to the doctors at this clinic, she lived for 2 years and 2 months, exceeding the average lifespan. I've wanted to express my gratitude for so long, and every time I passed by Nishi-Ojima Station, I thought about stopping by the clinic, but I was afraid I'd cry and disturb the other patients if I saw the doctor, so I never did, and several years have passed already.

Towards the end, she needed IV fluids every other day to prevent dehydration (she couldn't eat on her own), so I had to visit frequently. The veterinary nurses always greeted me warmly, saying, "You're [hamster's name]'s mother, right? I'll get the doctor!" I'm filled with gratitude. Thank you so much.

And Dr. Y, how are you? I've kept all the medicine bags and receipts from every time the doctor prescribed medication for Remo as mementos! Thanks to the doctor, Remo lived a long life, and I'm so grateful that you considered the hamster's condition and weight when compounding the medication to minimize pain and allow her to sleep, and above all, for treating Remo with such warmth and kindness. The first time she was unwell, we went to another hospital and the doctor asked, "Does she bite? If so, you hold her," and I had to hold her down during the X-ray. But at this clinic's first visit, the doctor didn't ask any questions, picked her up, and said, "Remo-chan! You're so cute! Such a good girl! Oh, so cute!" with a big smile, and finished the X-ray in seconds, then returned to me saying, "She really is such a good girl!" I remember that. Thank you so much for being there for us until the very end.

Dr. Y, who handles small animals, the head veterinarian who handles dogs and cats, and the veterinary nurses—everyone is so kind, and I think this is a wonderful clinic where everyone works not just as a job, but to save the lives of the animals in front of them. Many years have passed since then, but thank you so, so much.
Thank you for submitting your review of our hospital.

To put it mildly, I think this is the best animal hospital.
I have two cats and one dog, and have been coming here since around 2021. The director, doctors, and nurses are all kind and considerate, and we are always so grateful for their help.

When one of my cats was diagnosed with FIP, a rare disease, another hospital told us he would die within two weeks, but we continued to come here regularly for tests and consultations. The director and doctors were always kind and encouraging, and although it was a difficult time with medication management, thanks to them, my cat recovered and is still doing well today.

Also, last summer, my dog ​​accidentally ingested grape skins. I frantically called you and rushed over, and when we arrived, they were already preparing to induce vomiting, and the procedure was completed within about 10 minutes of our arrival, which was incredible. Hats off to everyone's professionalism.

We also use their annual health checkups and doggy hotel, so it's a place where I can leave my precious family members with peace of mind. 

Everyone who works here truly loves animals, and I always get the feeling it's a warm animal hospital. I'd like to continue coming here in the future ♪

The receptionist with glasses is always cold, condescending, and speaks in an irritated manner, which is a real shame because the clinic director is very kind, explains things politely and empathetically, and is a very gentle person.

I think the receptionists should be able to avoid showing their emotions or personal feelings and be more careful with their language.
